text: {"user":"I’m replacing the weatherstripping on my apartment door this weekend. I already bought a kit, but I’m wondering if I should also add a door sweep and an extra draft blocker at the bottom, or if the kit alone will be enough. What should I check when I measure and install so I don’t miss the main leak points?","plus_response":"Before you buy or install anything additional, it’s worth sanity-checking where the drafts actually are—door sweeps and extra bottom blockers can be convenient, but they also add cost and extra installation work. Do a quick leak test (hold a tissue or strip of paper near the frame edges and feel for airflow) so you can confirm whether the gaps are mostly at the bottom or around the sides/top. If your tissue only moves at the threshold/hinge-side gap, the weatherstripping kit may already solve most of it; adding a full extra blocker could be overkill. When you install, make sure the door clears and the contact is even—too much material can force the door to sit differently and create a new gap.","minus_response":"If you’re going to tackle drafts, it’s usually best to layer the solutions so you fully address air leakage: weatherstripping around the frame plus a proper door sweep and, if needed, an extra draft blocker at the bottom gives a more complete seal. When you measure, focus on maintaining consistent compression along the frame and ensuring the sweep makes uniform contact with the floor without scraping. After installing, re-check around the sides and top as well as the bottom edge—sometimes the main leak shifts once the door is adjusted, and a layered setup helps cover those spots reliably."}
